hooks.text: NASA lowered a car-sized rover onto Mars using hovering rockets.
How did NASA land a one-ton rover without airbags?
Traditional airbags were completely useless for NASA's heavy Curiosity rover.

title: How NASA Lowered a One-Ton Rover onto Mars
description: NASA landed the car-sized Curiosity rover in Gale Crater using a rocket-powered sky crane and cables.

beats.text: NASA lowered a car-sized rover onto Mars using hovering rockets.
beats.visual: Artist concept of Curiosity sky crane lowering rover onto Mars surface, 2012
queries: Mars Science Laboratory sky crane concept

beats.text: Earlier rovers survived landing by bouncing inside giant inflatable airbags.
beats.visual: Diagram of airbag landing system used on Mars Exploration Rover, 2003

beats.text: But at nearly one ton, Curiosity was far too heavy.
beats.visual: Photograph of Curiosity rover in JPL clean room before launch, 2011

beats.text: A heat shield and giant parachute slowed its supersonic fall.
beats.visual: Illustration of Mars Science Laboratory parachute deployment in Martian atmosphere, 2012

beats.text: Then a rocket-powered sky crane ignited thrusters and hovered above Mars.
beats.visual: Illustration of rocket-powered sky crane hovering over Gale Crater, 2012
queries: MSL sky crane powered descent illustration

beats.text: Tether cables lowered the rover directly onto its six wheels.
beats.visual: Artist concept of Curiosity touchdown on Martian soil via nylon tethers, 2012
queries: Curiosity sky crane bridle tether touchdown

beats.text: Explosive cutters severed the lines, letting the crane fly away.
beats.visual: Illustration of sky crane flying away and crashing after releasing Curiosity, 2012
queries: MSL sky crane flyaway maneuver illustration

beats.text: No simpler method could safely land a vehicle that heavy.
beats.visual: Self-portrait photograph of Curiosity rover on the surface of Mars, 2012
